result.title: CoTs remain monitorable when being unfaithful requires computation: Replicating and Extending the Necessity Effect Across Eleven Models
result.summary: While a LLM's chain of thought (CoT) is a promising approach to interpreting model outputs, prior work shows CoT's content does not always accurately reflect the reasoning process. Emmons et al. (2025) finds that models can follow a question hint without revealing so in its chain of thought, but when the hint is sufficiently complex the computation is forced into the CoT. This claim, however, has only been tested on Gemini models, and the datasets and code is closed source. We replicate their proxy task across eleven models from six families and find the necessity effect generalizes. Every model follows simple cues above a no-hint baseline, while concealed complex-cue following falls back near baseline for most models. We also extend the study from Emmons et al. (2025) to measure CoT-necessity and unfaithfulness across five cue families (four of them new) and three difficulty levels. The relationship between when CoT is necessary and unfaithfulness is task-specific and model-specific. For some hint types, models often verbalize their hint-following behavior even when the hint can be decoded in a single forward pass. These results support the case for CoT monitoring when unsafe behavior requires non-trivial computation, and that properties of CoT unfaithfulness are sensitive to model and setting.

AI.brief_summary: 复制并扩展 Emmons 等人的 CoT「必要性效应」实验：在 6 个家族共 11 个模型上，用 5 类提示线索与 3 个难度等级测量 CoT 必要性（计算是否被迫写入推理轨迹）与不忠实性，发现简单线索大多被隐蔽遵循、复杂线索的隐蔽遵循会回落到无提示基线附近。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「计算是否被迫进入显式轨迹」的线索类型与难度操纵范式，可能可供核查 VLM 推理中答案是否真正使用视觉/latent 内容、以及视觉旁路与信息坍缩下的可监控性问题；纯文本设置，迁移需自行核查。
